description:
Evaluate the inter-radicular space between the lower right canine (#27) and first premolar (#28) for a potential TAD (Temporary Anchorage Device) placement.

Context: An orthodontist needs to place a mini-screw between these roots to distalize the canine. You must determine if there is enough safety clearance (> 3.0 mm) between the roots at the mid-root level.

Steps:
1. The Blue Sky Plan project 'Mandible_Demo.bsp' is loaded.
2. Adjust the 3D view to visualize the *roots* of the teeth inside the bone. You must use the Volume Rendering settings (Density/Transparency) or the Cut/Clipping tools so the roots are clearly visible through the cortical bone.
3. Navigate to the space between tooth #27 and #28.
4. Use the Distance measurement tool to measure the narrowest horizontal distance between the roots at approximately the mid-root level (approx. 5mm below the crest).
5. Take a screenshot of your measurement view, clearly showing the roots and the measurement line.
6. Create a report file at 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\tad_safety_report.txt' with the format:
   Measurement: X.X mm
   Conclusion: [Safe/Risky]
   (Safe if > 3.0mm, Risky if <= 3.0mm)
